questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘RAJ’ is coded as ‘87’ and ‘GITA’ is coded as ‘148’. How will ‘VARUN’ be coded in that language?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain code language, ‘RAJ’ is coded as ‘87’ and ‘GITA’ is coded as ‘148’. How will ‘VARUN’ be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is :

Sum of the positional values of the letters × total number of the letter = number.

RAJ → Total number of letter is 3.

R(18) + A(1) + J(10) = 18 + 1 + 10 = 29

Sum of the positional values of the letters × total number of the letter = number

29 × 3 = 87

And,

GITA → Total number of letter is 4.

G(7) + I(9) + T(20) + A(1) = 7 + 9 + 20 + 1 = 37

Sum of the positional values of the letters × total number of the letter = number

37 × 4 = 148

Similarly,

VARUN → Total number of letter is 5.

V(22) + A(1) + R(18) + U(21) + N(14) = 22 + 1 + 18 + 21 + 14 = 76

Sum of the positional values of the letters × total number of the letter = number

76 × 5 = 380

Hence, VARUN will be written as “380”.

questions.question: The monthly income of three cricketers Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan, from different sources, are in the ratio of 12 : 9 : 7, and their expenditures are in the ratio 15 : 9 : 8. If Ankit saves 25% of his income for future investments, what is the ratio of the savings of Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan?
questions.questionHtml: The monthly income of three cricketers Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan, from different sources, are in the ratio of 12 : 9 : 7, and their expenditures are in the ratio 15 : 9 : 8. If Ankit saves 25% of his income for future investments, what is the ratio of the savings of Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Income ratio of  Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan is respectively: 12x : 9x : 7x

Expenditures ratio of  Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan is respectively: 

15y : 9y : 8y

FORMULA:

Savings = Income - Expenditures

CALCULATION:

Saving ratio of  Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan is respectively:

 (12x - 15y) : (9x - 9y) : (7x - 8y)

[Saving ratio = Income ratio - Ependiture ratio]

Ankit saves 25% of his income, So saving of Ankit is

12x - 15y = 25% of 12x

⇒ 12x - 15y = \(\frac{1}{4}\) × 12x

⇒ 12x - 15y = 3x

⇒ 9x = 15y

⇒ \(\frac{x}{y}\) = \(\frac{15}{9}\)

 ⇒ \(\frac{x}{y}\) = \(\frac{5}{3}\) (divided by 3)

So, x = 5; y = 3

Put the value of x and y saving of Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan,

(12x -15y) : (9x - 9y) : (7x - 8y)

⇒ (12 × 5 - 15 × 3) : (9 × 5 – 9 × 3) : (7 × 5 - 8 × 3)

⇒ (60 - 45) : (45 - 27) : (35 - 24)

⇒ 15 : 18 : 11

Hence, ‘15 : 18 : 11’ is the ratio of the savings of Ankit, Sanjay and Roshan.

questions.question: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the equation correct. 45 * 24 * 72 * 20 * 12 * 7
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the equation correct.

45 * 24 * 72 * 20 * 12 * 7
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule

Given equation 45 * 24 * 72 * 20 * 12 * 7

Option 1 : Using the combination ×, ÷, =, –, +

45 × 24 ÷ 72 = 20 - 12 + 7

By BODMAS rule

45 × 0.334 = 20 - 12 + 7

15 = 20 - 12 + 7

15 = 27 – 12

15 = 15 (LHS = RHS)

Option 2 : Using combination ÷, ×, +, –, =

45 ÷ 24 × 72 + 20 - 12 = 7

1.875 × 72 + 20 - 12 = 7

135 + 20 - 12 = 7

155 - 12 = 7

143 = 7 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3 : Using the combination =, ×, +, ÷, –

45 = 24 × 72 + 20 ÷ 12 - 7

45 = 24 × 72 + 1.67 – 7

45 = 1729.67 - 7

45 = 1722.67 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4 : Using the combination +, ÷, –, =, ×

45 + 24 ÷ 72 - 20 = 12 × 7

45 + 0.334 - 20 = 12 × 7

45 + 0.334 - 20 = 84

45.334 - 20 = 84

25.334 = 84 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is “×, ÷, =, –, +”.

A demand curve is the graphical presentation of the relationship between the price and the quantity demanded of a commodity.

questions.question: Fourteen persons can do a work in 18 days. After 5 days of work, 6 workers left the work, and joined back on the last day of the work. In how many days the work got completed?
questions.questionHtml: Fourteen persons can do a work in 18 days. After 5 days of work, 6 workers left the work, and joined back on the last day of the work. In how many days the work got completed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = 14 × 18 = 252 units.

Work done in first 5 days = 14 × 5 = 70 units.

Work done on last day (all 14 present) = 14 × 1 = 14 units.

Remaining work = 252 − (70 + 14) = 168 units.

Days with 8 workers = 168 ÷ 8 = 21 days.

Total days = 5 + 21 + 1 = 27 days.

∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial workers = 14, Initial days = 18. Workers left = 6. Joining back = Last day.

Formula Used: Total Work = Number of Persons × Number of Days

⇒ Total Work = 14 × 18 = 252 units

⇒ Work in first 5 days = 14 × 5 = 70 units

⇒ Work on the very last day (all returned) = 14 × 1 = 14 units

⇒ Work remaining for the middle period = 252 − 70 − 14 = 168 units

⇒ Number of workers in middle period = 14 − 6 = 8 workers

⇒ Time for middle period = 168 ÷ 8 = 21 days

⇒ Total time taken = 5 (initial) + 21 (middle) + 1 (last) = 27 days

∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Additional Information

Man-Days Concept

The total work is always constant and is calculated as the product of the number of men and the number of days (M1D1 = M2D2).

Work Equivalence Formula

For varying number of people over different periods: Total Work = (m1 × d1) + (m2 × d2) + ... + (mn × dn).

questions.question: An article is marked 27% above its cost price. If x% discount is allowed on the marked price and still there is a profit of 6.68%, then is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: An article is marked 27% above its cost price. If x% discount is allowed on the marked price and still there is a profit of 6.68%, then is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price = 27% above the cost price

After giving x% discount on marked price there is still a profit of 6.68%

Concept used:

S.P. = C.P. × [(100 + gain%)/100] (S.P. = Selling price, C.P.= Cost price)

S.P. = [M.P. – (M.P. × Discount %)] (M.P. = Marked price)

Calculation:

Let the C.P. of the article be Rs. 100 units.

So,

The S.P. of the article is = [(100 + 6.68)/100] × 100

⇒ 106.68 units

The M.P. of the article is = [100x + (100x × 27%)]

⇒ 100 + 27

⇒ 127 units

Now,

The S.P. of the article is = [127 - (127 × x%)] = 106.68

⇒ 127 - 127x/100 = 106.68

⇒ 127 – 1.27x = 106.68

⇒ 1.27x = 127 -106.68

⇒ x = 20.32/1.27

⇒ x = 16

∴ The value of x is 16.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers A and B is 5 : 8. If 5 is added to each of A and B, then the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The difference in A and B is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of two numbers A and B is 5 : 8. If 5 is added to each of A and B, then the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The difference in A and B is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial ratio of A : B is 5 : 8 (Difference = 3 units).

Final ratio after adding 5 is 2 : 3 (Difference = 1 unit).

To make the differences equal, multiply the second ratio by 3: (2 : 3) × 3 = 6 : 9.

Change in each part is 1 unit (from 5 to 6 or 8 to 9), which equals the added value 5.

Difference in A and B = 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15.

∴ The correct answer is 15.

Alternate Method

Given: Ratio A : B = 5 : 8 and the ratio becomes 2 : 3 when 5 is added to both.

Formula: If numbers are in ratio a : b, they can be taken as ax and bx.

Let the two numbers A and B be 5x and 8x respectively.

⇒ (5x + 5) / (8x + 5) = 2 / 3

⇒ 3 × (5x + 5) = 2 × (8x + 5)

⇒ 15x + 15 = 16x + 10

⇒ 16x − 15x = 15 − 10

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Number A = 5 × 5 = 25

⇒ Number B = 8 × 5 = 40

⇒ Difference = 40 − 25 = 15

∴ The correct answer is 15.

Additional Information

Ratio Difference Logic

When the same quantity is added to or subtracted from both terms of a ratio, the absolute difference between the parts remains proportional to the value added/subtracted.

Proportion Rule

If a/b = c/d, then ad = bc. This cross-multiplication is the standard algebraic way to solve ratio change problems.

Equating Parts

To solve ratio problems quickly, always aim to make the ratio difference consistent between the initial and final states by multiplying with a suitable constant.

Given:

A sold an article to B at a profit of 25%.

B sold it to C at a profit of 15%.

The profit made by B is Rs. 40 less than the profit made by A.

Concept used:

Profit = S.P. – C.P. (S.P. = Selling price, C.P.= Cost price)

S.P. = C.P. + (C.P. × profit%)

Calculation:

Let A bought the article for Rs.100x 

A sold it to B at [100x + (100x × 25%)] = Rs.125x

Profit earned by A = (125x – 100x) = Rs. 25x

So,

B bought the article for Rs. 125x 

B sold it to C at [125x + (125x × 15%)] = 143.75x

Profit earned by B = (143.75x – 125x) = Rs. 18.75x

According to the question,

25x – 18.75x = 40

⇒ 6.25x = 40

⇒ x = 6.4

So,

A bought the article for (100 × 6.4) = 640 Rs.

∴ The cost price (in Rs.) of the article for A is 640.

So ΔPAB will be an equilateral triangle.

Confusion PointsThere is a mistake in the question in this official paper because we get different answers by taking ΔAPM and ΔAPO.

We know that the radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent. Hence ΔAPO is also a right-angled triangle. So in ΔAPO,

tan 30° = OA/AP

⇒ 1/√3 = 13/PA 

⇒ AP = 13√3 which is not given in the options.

Additional InformationConditions for similarity of triangles:

Angle-Angle-Angle: If in two triangles, corresponding angles are equal, then their corresponding sides are in the same ratio (or proportion), and hence both triangles are similar.

SSS (Side-Side-Side): If in two triangles, the sides of one triangle are equal to are proportional to the sides, then their corresponding angles are equal, and hence both triangles are similar.

SAS (Side-Angle-Side): If the angles of a triangle are equal and the sides including these angles are proportional, then both triangles are identical.

questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. According to his hypothesis, now known as the neuron theory, each nerve cell communicates with others through contiguity rather than continuity.

B. The watershed of all studies of the nervous system was an observation made in 1889 by Spanish scientist Santiago Ramón y Cajal.

C. It has since been proved that Cajal’s theory is not universally true, but his central idea has remained an accurate guiding principle for all further study.

D. That is, communication between adjacent but separate cells must take place across the space and barriers separating them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC.'

Key Points

  • The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "an observation by Spanish scientist Santiago Ramón y Cajal". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
  • Sentence A will come after B as it is explaining the observation made by the scientist i.e. the neuron theory.
  • Sentence D will come after A as it is further explaining the neuron theory.
  • The sentence 'C' is the concluding part because it is talking about the final output of the theory.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: The watershed of all studies of the nervous system was an observation made in 1889 by Spanish scientist Santiago Ramón y Cajal. According to his hypothesis, now known as the neuron theory, each nerve cell communicates with others through contiguity rather than continuity. That is, communication between adjacent but separate cells must take place across the space and barriers separating them. It has since been proved that Cajal’s theory is not universally true, but his central idea has remained an accurate guiding principle for all further study.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. Ranbir could not went / to the award ceremony / as he was busy / shooting / for a film / in the Maldives.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

Ranbir could not went / to the award ceremony / as he was busy / shooting / for a film / in the Maldives.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Ranbir could not went' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the past tense form of the verb 'went' is incorrect.
  • The verb 'could' in the given sentence is a modal verb.
  • The modal verb 'could' is followed by the main verb and the main verb also stays in its base form.
  • Also, the main verb that is used with 'could' does not change form according to the subject.
  • Therefore, the base form of the verb 'go' should be used in place of the past tense form of the verb 'went'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: Ranbir could not go to the award ceremony as he was busy shooting for a film in the Maldives.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में क्रिया 'went' का भूतकाल रूप गलत है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में क्रिया 'could' एक modal verb है।
  • Modal verb 'could' के बाद मुख्य क्रिया आती है और मुख्य क्रिया भी अपने मूल रूप में रहती है।
  • साथ ही जिस मुख्य क्रिया के साथ 'could' प्रयोग किया जाता है, वह विषय के अनुसार रूप नहीं बदलता है।
  • इसलिए, भूतकाल क्रिया 'went' के स्थान पर मूल रूप क्रिया 'go' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: Ranbir could not go to the award ceremony as he was busy shooting for a film in the Maldives.

Key Points

Hinglish

  • दिए गए रेखांकित खण्ड में phrasal verb ''pulled out'' गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य एक पुराने भवन को गिराए जाने के बाद कार्य की प्रगति का सर्वेक्षण करने वाले ठेकेदार के बारे में बात कर रहा है।
  • Phrasal verb ''pulled out'' का अर्थ है कार आदि का सड़क के किनारे से आगे बढ़ जाना।
  • इसलिए, phrasal verb ''pulled out'' के स्थान पर phrasal verb ''pulled down'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • Phrasal verb ''pulled down'' का अर्थ है एक इमारत को ध्वस्त करना।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The professor told the media persons that from their research they had come to the conclusion that there was life on that planet.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is a direct speech.
  • The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
    • The commas, inverted commas are removed, and 'that' is added.
    • The first-person pronoun ''our'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''their'', the first-person pronoun ''we'' becomes the third-person pronoun ''they''.
    • The present perfect tense format 'Subject + have + V3 (come) + Object' will be changed into the past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (come) + Object'.
    • The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (is) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (was) + Object'.
       

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Additional Information

  • The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-
    Direct Speech Indirect Speech
    Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object) Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1+ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject+had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य direct speech है।
  • Direct speech को indirect speech में बदलने या बदलने के लिए बुनियादी नियम:
    • Commas, inverted commas हटा दिए जाते हैं और 'that' जोड़ा जाता है।
    • The first-person pronoun ''our'', third-person pronoun ''their'' बन जाता है, first-person pronoun ''we'' third-person pronoun ''they'' बन जाता है।
    • Present perfect tense format 'Subject + have + V3 (come) + Object' को past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (come) + Object' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • Present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (is) + Object' को past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (was) + Object' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
       

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The apple a day keeps the doctor away.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.

The apple a day keeps the doctor away.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'An apple a day.'

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the noun 'apple' is not a specified noun.
    • The listener doesn't know what apple you're talking i.e. any apple.
  • 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, which means that they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
    • We use 'a' before a consonant sound and we use 'an' before a vowel sound (here, apple).
  • The definite article 'the' is used before singular and plural nouns when the noun is specific or particular.
  • ''No article'' is used when we refer to general ideas, plurals, or uncountable nouns.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Sentence: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

Additional Information

There are three articles: a, an, and the. Articles are used before nouns or noun equivalents and are a type of adjective.

RULES COUNT NOUNS NON-COUNT NOUNS
Specific identity not known a, an (no article)
Specific identity is known the the
All things or things in general (no article) (no article)
 

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खंड में, संज्ञा 'apple'  निर्दिष्ट संज्ञा नहीं है।
    • श्रोता नहीं जानता कि आप किस सेब की बात कर रहे हैं।
  • 'A' और 'an' अनिश्चितकालीन लेख हैं, जिसका अर्थ है कि वे एक अनिर्दिष्ट संज्ञा को संदर्भित करते हैं, या पेश करते हैं।
    • हम एक consonant sound से पहले 'a' का उपयोग करें, और हम एक vowel sound (यहां, apple) से पहले 'an' का उपयोग करें।
  • निश्चित लेख 'the' का प्रयोग एकवचन और बहुवचन संज्ञाओं से पहले किया जाता है जब संज्ञा विशिष्ट या विशेष होती है।
  • जब हम सामान्य विचारों, बहुवचनों या बेशुमार संज्ञाओं का उल्लेख करते हैं तो ''No article'' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
     

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

सही वाक्य: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

questions.question: Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: Laxmi: “Dad, I need to speak to you.” Dad: “Yes, tell me.” Laxmi: “Please buy me a scooter.” Dad: “I think you are still too young for it.”

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).

Hinglish

  • इसलिए बहुवचन क्रिया 'have' के स्थान पर एकवचन क्रिया 'has' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।
